royce.claim: Patrick Mahomes is the best quarterback in the NFL, because best means who you hand January to.
supports: Playoff record and titles: 17-4 as a starter, three Super Bowl wins, three Super Bowl MVPs (F27, F15, F16)
Durability across seasons: no missed quarter of his team's games in his last 5 full seasons, 7 of 7 this season (F3)
This season's touchdown total, 14, plus how he plays: patient, careful with the ball, read as his eye test (F38)
royce.answer: The EPA rank is the objection. He grants it and says EPA prices a play, not a season, then backs Mahomes with the January record and the career résumé.

deacon.claim: Josh Allen is the best quarterback right now, because he is the top efficiency player who is actually playing.
supports: EPA per dropback: +0.29, 2nd of 35, on 241 dropbacks, against Mahomes at 10th (F32, F31)
Record and availability: 6-1 as a starter this season, every game played in each of his last 5 full seasons (F35, F6)
The tape read: he runs it and throws it deep, which explains why the points pile up, plus the 2024 MVP (F21)
deacon.answer: The objection is the 8-7 playoff record. He calls it a team result over a small number of starts, then points to the MVP and this season's efficiency.

lonnie.claim: Joe Burrow is the best quarterback right now, because his offense runs through his arm and he has been on the field every week.
supports: Volume and production: 23 touchdown passes and 290 dropbacks this season, EPA 7th of 35, ahead of Mahomes (F41, F34)
Role and fit: Cincinnati hands him the whole offense, and to his eye the ball comes out quick, a read tied to his 6-2 record (F37)
Playoff résumé: 5-2 as a starter, with 8 of 8 games played this season (F30, F13)
lonnie.answer: The objection is availability, with 2 of his last 5 full seasons missing a quarter of the games. He concedes it plainly and answers with this season, played in full, and the narrow gap between 6-1 and 6-2.

beats: Opening positions: Royce says Mahomes on January, Deacon says Allen on EPA, and Lonnie asks why not Lamar, who is first in EPA.
The sample and availability clash: Lamar is on injured reserve with 112 dropbacks, Burrow's injury years get pressed, and Royce hits Allen's 8-7 playoff record.
The trap: Lonnie says 6-1 and 6-2 don't separate this season, and Royce concedes it leaves January; then Lonnie pins Royce on Mahomes ranking 10th in EPA this season.
Decisive exchange: Royce reframes EPA as measuring a play, not a game, and gets pressed hard on 'best right now'. Final answers.
